audience_promise.novel_situation: A lone player enters an inexplicable portal in his private Minecraft world and encounters the same ravine at three connected moments of one history.
audience_promise.human_problem: He mistakes preserving the structures he authored for preserving his home, then must decide what deserves his remaining time when the known ruin arrives.
audience_promise.pressure_source: His younger and older selves act with unequal information while an ordinary fire spreads through geography made vulnerable by his hurried portal construction.
expected_pleasure: Recognising one location through altered block states and matched compositions
Reinterpreting fair visual clues as the protagonist becomes their cause
Solving the portal builder and ridge figure identities through action rather than exposition
Watching Minecraft resources and mechanics force a consequential rescue choice
audience_promise.disappointment_test: The promise fails if the portal becomes an ordinary Nether trip, the timeline invisibly corrects choices, the narrator lies, the fire is arbitrary, or the wolf survives without prior geography and mechanics enabling the rescue.

premise.disruption: A complete lit portal appears in a cave the protagonist knows was empty and to which no other player has access.
premise.difficult_goal: Identify the builder, return from displaced moments of the world and prevent the burned future without losing the wolf.
premise.central_opposition: Information-asymmetric versions of the protagonist pursue incompatible immediate aims while fixed evidence and spreading fire reduce his options.
premise.meaningful_consequence: His attempt to preserve the journey creates the ordinary hazard that destroys the homestead, but the foreknowledge also lets him save the wolf and redefine what preserving home means.
premise.logline: In a private survival world, a lone player enters an impossible portal and is thrown through different moments of his ravine; when he learns that he is the builder whose hurried work will ignite his home, he must preserve the journey that gives him foreknowledge and choose between saving the structure or his trapped wolf.

theme.subject: Agency inside irreversible events
theme.question: If an observed outcome cannot be rewritten, can a choice still matter?
theme.provisional_argument: Agency need not mean replacing every established fact; it can survive as the deliberate choice of which responsibility to carry through an irreversible loss.

characters.want: Solve who built the portal and prevent the destruction of his homestead.
characters.need: Distinguish recoverable structures from the living relationship that made the structure a home.
characters.fear: That his authorship gives him no control and that every choice merely completes a loss he has already seen.
characters.belief: If he maps every block state and preserves the correct plan, he can force a complete solution.
characters.limitation: He continues protecting a plan after its purpose changes and withholds decisive information when uncertainty threatens his control.
characters.strategy: Compare persistent geography, track construction signatures, leave a warning, reproduce the portal and use limited survival resources against the fire.
characters.contradiction: Curiosity makes him enter the portal, while later caution makes him recreate it and conceal the truth from himself.
characters.boundary: He will not knowingly abandon a living companion merely to protect replaceable blocks.
characters.pressure_point: The roof remains partly salvageable at the exact moment the seated wolf becomes trapped behind the burning yard.
characters.relationship_function: His bond with the wolf converts a temporal logic problem into a responsibility that can be chosen and visibly acted upon.
characters.agency: He enters, crosses again, avoids direct contact, leaves an incomplete marker, mines the obsidian, builds and lights the portal, lets his younger self enter, redirects the water, releases the wolf, recreates the silhouette and extinguishes the portal.

characters.want: Expressed behaviourally, to remain near and follow the protagonist when released.
characters.need: A reachable route out of the closed pen and an explicit release from its seated state.
characters.fear: Expressed behaviourally through retreat and distress around spreading fire.
characters.belief: No abstract belief is assigned; its trained behaviour is to wait when seated and follow when released.
characters.limitation: It cannot understand the red marker, open the gate or plan around temporal information.
characters.strategy: Wait in the familiar pen, then follow the protagonist through the cleared route.
characters.contradiction: Its reliable obedience makes it emotionally secure during ordinary life but physically vulnerable during the fire.
characters.boundary: It is not given human reasoning or used to solve the temporal mystery.
characters.pressure_point: Heat and a blocked yard prevent escape while the protagonist is still defending the roof.
characters.relationship_function: It embodies the living part of home and supplies a concrete alternative to preserving the structure.
characters.agency: Limited diegetic agency: once released, it responds and follows through the route rather than appearing safely elsewhere by convenience.

opposition.opposing_goal: The younger self seeks the apparent stranger and a way to change the ruin, while the older self seeks to keep that younger self on the journey; during the climax, the spreading fire consumes the structure faster than either plan can preserve it.
opposition.why_neither_side_can_withdraw: Without entering and crossing again, the younger self never gains the foreknowledge used in the rescue; without preserving that journey, the older self risks the only successful action he has evidence for.
opposition.advantage: The observed ruin supplies fixed evidence, the younger self is predictable to his older self, and the fire exploits a connected timber route hidden beneath the house.
opposition.vulnerability: The future image is incomplete rather than all-knowing, and the protagonist’s repeated movement and construction habits expose the identity of the apparent stranger.
opposition.cost_of_confrontation: Directly revealing the older self could make the younger self refuse the portal and abandon the only foreknowledge the older self trusts.
opposition.cost_of_avoidance: Silence lets the younger self experience apparent total loss, allows the fire hazard to mature and forces the rescue under maximum pressure.

stakes.immediate: Escape each temporal displacement and determine whether the world state is past or future.
stakes.practical: The homestead, stored resources, portal route and safe ravine access may be lost to fire.
stakes.personal: The protagonist’s confidence in his own authorship and judgement is dismantled.
stakes.relational: The seated wolf may die unless the protagonist abandons the structure and reaches it.
stakes.moral: He must decide whether to impose fear and incomplete information on his younger self to preserve a rescue he knows succeeds.
stakes.existential: He must act meaningfully despite evidence that the physical outcome cannot become a different event.
stakes.systemic: Limited by design to the causal intelligibility of one private world rather than a wider apocalypse.

story_layers.chronological_story: The homestead and wolf exist; the older traveller arrives shortly before discovery, leaves an incomplete marker, mines local obsidian, builds the portal and creates a flammable connection; the younger self enters; the connection carries fire to the house; the older self saves the wolf; at dawn he becomes the silhouette seen by the arriving younger self, who then crosses into the past.
story_layers.causal_plot: Exclusive authorship prompts entry; apparent loss prompts a second crossing; remembered interventions prove participation; that proof and the rescue motive prompt portal construction; hurried construction causes fire; fire forces the water-and-wolf choice; concealment of the rescued wolf motivates the earlier self to complete the loop.
story_layers.audience_presentation: The audience follows discovery, aftermath, pursuit, pre-discovery arrival, warning, construction, fire, rescue and the reverse-angle silhouette, learning causes after first seeing their effects.

ending_design.final_choice: Stop moving the single water source around the roof, place it in the eastern stone drain, reach the pen and release the wolf while accepting that the house will burn.
ending_design.climax_mechanism: A proposed ordinary Minecraft chain carries fire from lava to temporary spruce staging and connected timber supports; water can serve either dispersed structural defence or a concentrated rescue route, but time does not permit both.
ending_design.emotional_result: Grief for the unchanged home is joined by relief, responsibility and a morally uneasy understanding of why he concealed the rescue from himself.
ending_design.thematic_consequence: The outcome remains fixed while the meaning of the outcome changes through a choice that protects a living relationship.
ending_design.final_relationship_state: The wolf is no longer treated as one possession inside the homestead; it is the responsibility the protagonist deliberately carries beyond it.
ending_design.final_state: The homestead matches the burned future, the wolf is alive, the earlier self has crossed into the past, the older self continues forwards and the portal frame is unlit.
ending_design.final_image: At first light, the protagonist leads the wolf away from the burned west-rim homestead while the dark portal frame stands across the ravine.
ending_design.unresolved_serial_thread: None. The first origin of the portal’s copied temporal routing remains intentionally open as thematic residue, not a serial hook.

structure_choice.rationale: Five goal-driven movements track changes in audience knowledge and protagonist agency while allowing world chronology to fold around personal chronology without imposing fixed act percentages.

minecraft_story_engine.mechanic: Private-world authorship, persistent block states, a temporally redirected portal, local obsidian mining, lava ignition, fire spread, movable water, a seated tamed wolf and repeatable ravine geography.
minecraft_story_engine.causal_effect: The portal initiates displacement; the protagonist’s local mining and temporary staging physically create both the remembered frame details and the proposed fire route.
minecraft_story_engine.goal_or_strategy_effect: Persistent blocks let him date locations and construct warnings, while limited inventory makes one water source and local obsidian central to his plan.
minecraft_story_engine.conflict_effect: Timber connectivity allows a small construction shortcut to threaten the house, and the wolf’s seated state prevents convenient self-evacuation.
minecraft_story_engine.reversal_effect: The odd footing, marker and silhouette change from evidence of another player into evidence of the protagonist’s later actions; the empty pen changes from apparent death to incomplete viewpoint.
minecraft_story_engine.climactic_use: He relocates water from ineffective roof defence to the eastern stone drain, reaches the pen, releases the wolf and later uses the recovered source to extinguish the portal.
minecraft_story_engine.geography_effect: The west-rim house, north-wall cave, lower lava shelf, connected timber stair, eastern stone drain and ridge sight line determine ignition, pursuit, concealment and escape.
minecraft_story_engine.construction_as_character_action: The protagonist physically mines every portal block, copies the irregular frame he remembers and chooses expedient spruce staging, making construction an expression of control and the cause of later danger.

serial_engine.engine: Not applicable; the film resolves its central mystery, fire and relationship within one episode.
serial_engine.episode_resolution_rule: The portal builder, figure identity, fixed outcome and wolf’s fate must resolve before the final image; only the non-essential first origin of temporal routing may remain open.
